svg.aria-label: The cluster and the two paths through it. 54 workers reach the coordinator through PgBouncer for the work queue — thousands of tiny transactions — and reach the 9 data shards directly with binary COPY, because a pooler in a bulk byte path would become the bottleneck. The coordinator also reads the shards through postgres_fdw for analytics.
svg.text: Two paths, and the pooler is on only one of them
The asymmetry is the design: the control plane is many tiny transactions, the data plane is a sustained byte stream.
· thousands of tiny transactions · latency matters
· one sustained byte stream · throughput matters · NO POOLER
postgres_fdw · analytics only, never the bulk path
The pooler exists because the control plane is ~250,000 tiny UPDATEs over a run, every one on a worker's critical path — exactly what
transaction pooling is for. It is absent from the data plane for the opposite reason: PgBouncer is single-threaded, so putting it in front of
~700 MB/s of COPY traffic would make it the bottleneck. Sharding already holds each instance at 12 backends, so there is nothing left for a
